title: A nonzero first cohomology group forces a low-degree subcurve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be a proper reduced connected $k$-scheme of dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme, possibly empty, with ideal sheaf $I_Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. If $H^1(X,I_Z\otimes L)\ne0$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there is a nonempty reduced connected closed subcurve $B\subseteq X$ of dimension one such that
$$\deg_k(L|_B)\leq -2\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)+\dim_k\Gamma(Z\times_XB,\mathcal O_{Z\times_XB}).$$
Here restriction is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], the intersection is the scheme-theoretic fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], degree is the Euler-characteristic degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and $\chi$ is [def-pc-euler-characteristic].

source.place: Tag 0E3E, lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein, statement; the intersection degree is its finite k-scheme length.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $X$ is Noetherian and $L$ and $\mathcal O_X$ are coherent. In a Noetherian affine chart every ideal is finitely generated; its associated ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent, so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes all the closed-subscheme ideals below coherent. Tensoring with an invertible module is locally tensoring with the free module of rank one, hence preserves injections, quotients and coherence. A Noetherian space has finitely many irreducible components (otherwise Noetherian induction on closed subsets splits a minimal counterexample into two smaller counterexamples). Any zero-dimensional component would be a closed point disjoint from all other components, hence open as well as closed. Connectedness and $\dim X=1$ exclude it. Thus $X$ has pure dimension one.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), preparation for application of duality

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module] to $X$ and $\mathcal F=I_Z\otimes L$. A nonzero finite-dimensional vector space has a nonzero linear functional, by extending any nonzero vector to a basis and taking a coordinate. Hence the assumed nonzero $H^1$ gives a nonzero map $\varphi:I_ZL\to\omega_X$. Let $Y$ be the reduced union of precisely the irreducible components where its generic stalk map is nonzero. This is a finite union of closed components, of pure dimension one. It is nonempty: otherwise the generic-detection assertion of the cited node would give $\varphi=0$. Write $\mathcal J$ for its ideal.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), first two sentences: choose the nonzero dualizing map and its component support

proof.text: The restriction of $\varphi$ to $\mathcal JI_ZL$ vanishes at every component generic point: on $Y$ the stalk of $\mathcal J$ is zero, since $X$ is reduced, and outside $Y$ the stalk of $\varphi$ is zero by construction. Its image is therefore zero by [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. For local sections $j\in\mathcal J$ and $t\in I_ZL$, $j\varphi(t)=\varphi(jt)=0$. Thus $\varphi$ factors through $I_ZL/\mathcal JI_ZL$ with image in the annihilator of $\mathcal J$. The closed subscheme $Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Identify this annihilator with $i_*\omega_Y$ using [lem-sfb-closed-subcurve-dualizing-adjunction]. On $Y$ this gives $\psi:(I_ZL)|_Y\to\omega_Y$, nonzero at every component generic point.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), factor through the subcurve and identify its dualizing module

proof.text: Put $T=Z\times_XY$, $L_Y=L|_Y$ and $I'=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_T)$. On a local trivialization of $L$, with $I=I_Z$ and $J=\mathcal J$, the natural map $(I/JI)\otimes L_Y\twoheadrightarrow((I+J)/J)\otimes L_Y=I'L_Y$ is surjective. Its kernel $K$ is zero at every generic point of $Y$, since $Z$ has dimension zero and there $I=\mathcal O_X$. Kernels and cokernels here are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum]. The image of $K$ in $\omega_Y$ is zero by [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. Consequently $\psi$ descends to $\alpha:I'L_Y\to\omega_Y$; its generic stalk maps are still nonzero. Both generic stalks have dimension one, so these maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), replace the pulled-back ideal by the ideal of the scheme-theoretic intersection

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is injective. Indeed its kernel is a submodule of the invertible module $L_Y$ and has zero stalk at every component generic point. On any affine open trivializing $L_Y$, a section in this kernel is an element of a reduced ring that becomes zero at every minimal prime localization. It lies in every minimal prime, hence in the nilradical, and is zero. Its cokernel $Q$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] and is generically zero. A proper closed subset of a Noetherian pure one-dimensional scheme containing no component generic point is a finite set of closed points: intersect each of the finitely many irreducible components and use dimension one. Thus $Q$ has zero-dimensional support, and $0\to I'L_Y\to\omega_Y\to Q\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), injectivity after removal of the closed-point kernel, and support of the cokernel

proof.text: Choose any connected component $B$ of the nonempty $Y$. The finite component decomposition is open and closed, so restriction of the preceding exact sequence is exact and the restricted dualizing module represents the same $H^1$-dual functor on $B$ (extend a coherent module by zero to the other open-and-closed components). Hence it is $\omega_B$ by the uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. The reduced scheme $B$ has dimension one; it is closed in $X$ and proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Set $T_B=T\times_YB=Z\times_XB$, $L_B=L|_B$, $I_B=\ker(\mathcal O_B\to\mathcal O_{T_B})$, and $Q_B=Q|_B$. We have $0\to I_BL_B\to\omega_B\to Q_B\to0$, with $Q_B$ of zero-dimensional support.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), last sentence: work on a connected component before the Euler calculation

proof.text:
The quotient $\mathcal O_B/I_B$ is supported on $T_B$ and its global sections are $\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B})$, directly by the closed-pushforward definition. Apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] to this quotient and to $Q_B$: its tensor with $L_B$ has Euler characteristic $\dim_k\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B})$, and $\chi(Q_B)\ge0$. Additivity [lem-pc-euler-additive] for $0\to I_BL_B\to L_B\to L_B\otimes(\mathcal O_B/I_B)\to0$ gives
$\chi(I_BL_B)=\deg_k(L_B)+\chi(\mathcal O_B)-\dim_k\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B})$
by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Additivity for the exact sequence of step 6 and [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module] now give
$$0\le\chi(Q_B)=-2\chi(\mathcal O_B)-\deg_k(L_B)+\dim_k\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B}).$$
Rearranging is the required inequality for this $B$.
